units.laterEditorialCommentary: All notes pp.13–25 were read. They distinguish relative and conferred necessity; repeatedly criticize treating absences as causes; restrict cause to actual efficacy and distinguish capacity before action; quote Persian poetry on dependence; recast human agency as preparation; attribute the four determination theories to theologians; distinguish imaginary-time accounts; explain preference versus preponderance and the equal-path objection; discuss knowledge of benefits; and supply Asfar and Razi references. The editor's extensive disagreement with the causal account remains separate from Tabatabai's argument. The later claims about schools and underlying quoted works are attributed, not independently verified historical conclusions.

units.englishReviewFinding: All 23 English paragraphs were compared with all 31 stored Arabic paragraphs and the complete external unit. The translation preserves the two standpoints on divine proximity, the vertical causal qualification of human agency, and the distinction between necessity of a voluntary act and coercion. No English replacement is required. The phrase ‘acquire independence’ translates the early/base وتستقل and must be understood as dependent or relative independence through the Necessary, as the following sentence expressly qualifies it; the later editor's contrary wording is recorded rather than substituted.
variants: Later p. 266 nn. 8–9 changes early/base به تتقوم هذه الروابط وتستقل to بها تتقوم هذه الروابط ولم تستقل. The first change regularizes pronoun gender; the second reverses the affirmative verb on doctrinal grounds. The note continuing on p. 267 itself admits that the inherited affirmative can mean the relations' relative independence with respect to their own effects. Retain the early/base wording and its translation, with this explicit qualification in the apparatus.

Later p. 269 uses الذي معه بقية أجزاء العلة التامة for early/base التي معه بقية أجزاء العلة التامة; later p. 272 has وهي أنه صادر where early/base reads وهو أنه صادر. These are grammatical regularizations, not grounds for altering the base doctrinal text.

units.englishReviewFinding: All nine English paragraphs were compared with all ten Arabic paragraphs and the external witnesses. The distinction between providence in deficient agents and in the Necessary, and the causal ordering of intellectual, imaginal and material realms, are accurately preserved. units.englishReviewFinding: All 17 English paragraphs were compared with all 20 Arabic paragraphs and both external witnesses. The translation preserves evil as privation, the distinction between an injurious existent and the privation itself, the attributed objection and reply concerning pain, and primary versus secondary intention. In the summary of pain, English construes كمال تلك القوة as the object of فقدها: the soul apprehends its loss of the faculty's perfection. This is a plausible contextual construal of the unvocalized early wording, but differs from the current base's nominative mark كمالُ and from the later editor's parenthetical punctuation. That interpretive choice is now disclosed; no silent substantive emendation is proposed.
variants: Later p. 284 n. 4 explicitly changes early/base الذات التي يصيبه العدم to الذات التي يصيبها العدم. Retain the inherited body while recording the gender regularization.
Later p. 285 n. 1 changes early/base لعروض الأعدام to لعرض الأعدام. This is an editorial wording change; the original occurrence-language and its English rendering remain.

Early p. 312 and later p. 284 share the consonantal sequence تدرك النفس عنده فقدها كمال تلك القوة. The base marks كمالُ; later punctuation closes a parenthesis after فقدها and its n. 3 glosses the pronoun as the affliction. The current English instead understands the soul's loss of the faculty's perfection. Because the witnesses do not settle that syntactic difficulty, preserve the Arabic and explicitly identify the translation's construal rather than pretending agreement of all punctuation/vocalization.
Later p. 284 vocalizes وحدّه in منتزع من مرتبة الوجود وحدّه. The early print p. 312 and base have the same consonants; the English appropriately includes the limit of the existential degree.

Separate إيصالكلّ; join the accidentally divided كما لها as كمالها; repair بأصابة to بإصابة; and correct the first example's بشرَ to بشرّ. Early pp. 311–312 and later pp. 281–284 support the words; the last two are orthographic/diacritic normalization.
units.laterEditorialCommentary: All notes on pp. 282–286 were read, including attribution of the proof to Quṭb al-Dīn and Ṣadrā, three accounts of incidental evil and the long Mīr Dāmād quotation, attribution of the pain objection to al-Dawānī, and the complete quotation of Ṭabāṭabāʾī's Asfār annotation objecting to Ṣadrā's answer and proposing another distinction. The editor also records al-Sabzawārī's alternative, lexical/pronominal glosses, the mediated attribution of the fivefold division to Aristotle, and final bibliographical pointers. These disagreements are later contextual evidence; they are not used to rewrite the argument actually printed in Nihāyat. Underlying source works were not independently collated.

units.bodyOutcome: The complete body is represented in both languages. Propose five Arabic replacements: two diacritic repairs, infinity-expression spelling/spacing, restoration of موجدة from both external witnesses, and the explicit later correction موجودا in the causal contrast. One English sentence is corrected to match the restored existence-bestowing cause. All substantial later editorial interventions are distinguished from inherited text.
units.englishReviewFinding: All 25 English paragraphs and the existing note were compared with all 31 Arabic paragraphs and both complete witnesses. The translation accurately preserves the distinction between the possibility-of-the-nobler principle and the stronger claim of a separate same-quiddity archetype, including all three objections and the exception for human development. Change ‘Every existent cause’ to ‘Every cause that bestows existence’ to match early/later موجدة against the base's موجودة. The English ‘existing in another’ already follows the correct contextual reading موجودا in the second proof; the proposed Arabic correction makes that interpretive repair explicit. The remaining English and existing note are retained.
variants: Early p. 319 and later p. 294 read كل علة موجدة واجدة لجميع كمالات المعلول; base has موجودة. Restore موجِدة and correct the corresponding English from an ‘existent cause’ to a cause that bestows existence. This is supported by both external witnesses, not merely by doctrinal inference.

Early p. 320 and base read موجدا في غيره; later p. 297 n. 1 explicitly corrects this to موجودا في غيره. The immediate contrast with موجودا في نفسه and the account of relational existence support adoption of the missing-wāw correction. Record the early reading; do not present the corrected wording as unanimously attested. English had already rendered ‘existing in another’.

Early p. 316 has الذي هذه صفتها; base already reads صفته, which the later editor explicitly adopts at p. 290 n. 4. Early p. 317 has تصح صدور الكثير منه, base يصح صدور الكثير منه, and later p. 291 تصحح صدور الكثير منه. The base's existing grammatical repair is retained; no importation of the later reformulation is needed. Later p. 292 also regularizes يفي to تفي.

Later p. 293 adds هو in جسم هو موضوعها (n. 2), changes قيامه to قيامها (n. 3), and changes يعتني به ويوجده ويدبر أمره to feminine plurals (n. 5). The last note admits the inherited masculine pronouns can refer to كل منها. Retain the early/base text and intelligible English. Later p. 294 also has فتكون where early/base has فيكون.

Later p. 295 n. 1 inserts [معقولنا] after يكون and identifies it as an editorial addition absent from its copies. No corresponding Arabic insertion is made here; English already makes the understood referent intelligible.

Later p. 296 n. 3 changes يوجد to يصدر on the basis of al-Asfār; n. 6 changes بواسطة to بواسطته. Retain the early p. 320/base wording in the attributed argument; the underlying Asfār was not independently collated. Later p. 297 changes تكون to يكون in the two discussions of a جهة, and p. 298 nn. 2–3 changes كمالها / لكونها to كماله / لكونه. These grammatical regularizations are recorded but not imported.
Repair تتصورّ to تتصوّر and يدبرّ to يدبّر, and normalize لايتناهي بما لا يتناهي to لا يتناهى بما لا يتناهى. These affect only diacritics, spacing and the clear verb's final letter.
units.laterEditorialCommentary: Read every note on pp. 290–298, including the claim that the quiddity clause is redundant, Peripatetic and Illuminationist bibliographies, the quoted attribution of Platonic Forms, all three argument attributions, the explanation of reality/attenuated-reality predication, the long Ṣadrā quotation on the history and uses of the principle and its continuation onto p. 296, the source-driven corrections, and the final-objection bibliography. Historical attributions and underlying quotations remain attributed later evidence; none implies independent verification of the cited works.

coverage.finding: Read intrinsic origination first through quiddity and then through fundamental relational existence, including the whole/parts conclusion; early pp. 323–324 and later pp. 303–304.

units.bodyOutcome: The complete early/base body is retained. The later editor's directional and grammatical changes in the definition of temporal priority/posteriority are explicitly recorded. No missing original passage or source reference was found.
units.englishReviewFinding: All fourteen English paragraphs were compared with all seventeen Arabic paragraphs and both external witnesses. Intrinsic dependence is distinguished from temporal origination through continuous substantial motion; the author's own account is kept separate from the theologians' view being criticized. In the time-definition sentence, ‘adjoining’ is the existing conservative rendering of تليه in both clauses. The context requires the actuality after a potentiality and the potentiality before an actuality; the later editor makes that asymmetry explicit. The inherited Arabic is not silently rewritten, and the apparatus discloses this issue. No English body replacement is proposed.
variants: Early p. 324 and base read وقبليته هي كونه قوة للفعلية التي تليه وبعديته هي كونه فعلية للقوة التي تليه. Later p. 304 n. 2 changes the first تليه to تليها; n. 3 changes the second التي تليه to التي تسبقها. Both notes propose still fuller formulations giving each term its relation to both neighbours. Retain the early/base sentence; English ‘adjoining’ reflects adjacency without silently claiming the later wording is the original. The contextual order is potentiality before its actualization, as the preceding paragraph expressly states.
Later p. 306 n. 3 changes عروض التغير to عرض التغير. Retain early p. 326/base عروض and the English ‘occurrence of change’.

The phrase متحول من القوة lacks an explicit إلى الفعل in early p. 324, base, and later p. 304. The English ‘passes out of potentiality’ accurately preserves this shorter wording; no unsupported phrase is supplied.
units.laterEditorialCommentary: Read every note on pp. 303–306: internal references and the gloss of intrinsic coexistent nonexistence, the two time-definition corrections and suggested expansions, and the distinction between merely imagined time without a ground of abstraction and supposed abstracted time grounded in divine permanence. The editor's attributions to theologians, Ashʿarites, al-Sabzawārī and Ṭabāṭabāʾī's Asfār notes remain attributed commentary, with no independent collation of those works claimed.

units.bodyOutcome: The complete final chapter and authorial colophon are present. Restore معدّات in place of the base's متعدّات, supported by both external witnesses. Retain and document the later editor's additional word and grammatical correction rather than silently importing them.
units.englishReviewFinding: All six English paragraphs were compared with all seven Arabic paragraphs and the entire external final unit. The distinction between perpetual divine bestowal and an unchanging or recurring natural world is accurately preserved. The English ‘preparatory factors’ already translates the external reading معدّات correctly. The authorial completion date, 6 Muḥarram 1395 AH, and closing blessing are complete. The sentence saying the ancient views have ‘now’ been overturned is the author's historical statement, not a new scientific assessment by this edition. No English replacement is needed.
variants: Early p. 326 and later p. 308 read شرائط ومعدات مجهولة لنا; the base has ومتعدّات. Restore ومعدّات. This removes an intrusive tāʾ in the technical term for preparatory factors; the existing English already reflects the correct word.
Later p. 308 inserts [مأخوذة] after أصولا موضوعة and its n. 1 expressly says the bracketed word is absent from its copies. It is not added to the early/base body.
Later p. 308 n. 2 changes early/base انفسخ اليوم هذه الآراء to انفسخت اليوم هذه الآراء. Retain the inherited wording and record this grammatical regularization.

The author's colophon is dated 6 Muḥarram 1395 in both external witnesses and the base. The later editor's distinct notes give completion dates for his own work of 27 Rajab 1416 and Shawwāl 1423 and sign ʿAbbās ʿAlī al-Zāriʿī al-Sabzawārī. These later dates are not authorial revision dates or replacements for the book's colophon.
units.laterEditorialCommentary: Read the internal reference to XII.13, the full discussion of cycles and the Illuminationist position on preserved celestial images, the attribution of permanence to earlier philosophers with Ṣadrā's reported rejection of that attribution, both explicit editorial interventions, and the editor's complete closing account. Underlying Ḥikmat al-Ishrāq, al-Milal wa-l-niḥal and al-Asfār passages were not independently collated. The author's end is distinguished from the editor's devotional conclusion and dated statement of work.
units.omissionsAndFootnotes: No original note or concluding passage is absent. The full authorial colophon, including day, month, year and blessing, is represented in both languages. The later editorial ending was read and excluded from the author's body; the following index boundary on p. 309 confirms the extent of the later unit.

The complete final chapter and authorial colophon are present. Restore معدّات in place of the base's متعدّات, supported by both external witnesses. Retain and document the later editor's additional word and grammatical correction rather than silently importing them.

All six English paragraphs were compared with all seven Arabic paragraphs and the entire external final unit. The distinction between perpetual divine bestowal and an unchanging or recurring natural world is accurately preserved. The English ‘preparatory factors’ already translates the external reading معدّات correctly. The authorial completion date, 6 Muḥarram 1395 AH, and closing blessing are complete. The sentence saying the ancient views have ‘now’ been overturned is the author's historical statement, not a new scientific assessment by this edition. No English replacement is needed.

Early p. 326 and later p. 308 read شرائط ومعدات مجهولة لنا; the base has ومتعدّات. Restore ومعدّات. This removes an intrusive tāʾ in the technical term for preparatory factors; the existing English already reflects the correct word.

Later p. 308 inserts [مأخوذة] after أصولا موضوعة and its n. 1 expressly says the bracketed word is absent from its copies. It is not added to the early/base body.

Later p. 308 n. 2 changes early/base انفسخ اليوم هذه الآراء to انفسخت اليوم هذه الآراء. Retain the inherited wording and record this grammatical regularization.

The author's colophon is dated 6 Muḥarram 1395 in both external witnesses and the base. The later editor's distinct notes give completion dates for his own work of 27 Rajab 1416 and Shawwāl 1423 and sign ʿAbbās ʿAlī al-Zāriʿī al-Sabzawārī. These later dates are not authorial revision dates or replacements for the book's colophon.

Later editorial commentary: Read the internal reference to XII.13, the full discussion of cycles and the Illuminationist position on preserved celestial images, the attribution of permanence to earlier philosophers with Ṣadrā's reported rejection of that attribution, both explicit editorial interventions, and the editor's complete closing account. Underlying Ḥikmat al-Ishrāq, al-Milal wa-l-niḥal and al-Asfār passages were not independently collated. The author's end is distinguished from the editor's devotional conclusion and dated statement of work.

Original-note and boundary review: No original note or concluding passage is absent. The full authorial colophon, including day, month, year and blessing, is represented in both languages. The later editorial ending was read and excluded from the author's body; the following index boundary on p. 309 confirms the extent of the later unit.
